newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates steady at 3.05 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates steady at 3.05 percent.

text.p: German call money rates remained at about 3.05 percent in midday dealings on Thursday despite what traders said were rising deposits by commercial banks at the Bundesbank ahead of the weekend.
Traders expected little movement in call money rates ahead of the weekend due to the relatively high reserve levels.
The Bundesbank said reserves rose to 41.6 billion marks as of Wednesday from 40 billion on Tuesday, while the monthly average remained at 40.6 billion marks.
The steady rates came despite the Bundesbank on Wednesday draining 1.9 billion marks from the banking system. Traders had expected a relatively neutral repo allocation.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average on Thursday was slightly lower at 3.06933 compared with 3.08533 percent on Wednesday.
Term money rates, however, were on the rise as the 12-month FIBOR rate rose to 3.35467 percent from 3.33100 percent on Wednesday.
